about: The priest offers the host to God the Father for his own sins, offenses, and negligences, for all who are present, and for all faithful Christians, living and dead. He asks that the offering may avail both him and them unto salvation and eternal life.

seg.nr: At solemn Mass the deacon hands the celebrant the paten with the Host. At low Mass the priest takes it himself and offers it while saying the prayer.

seg.tr: Holy Father, almighty and eternal God, receive this unblemished sacrificial offering, which I, Your unworthy servant, offer to You, my living and true God, for my countless sins, offenses, and omissions, for all those present, and also for all the Christian faithful, living and departed, so that it may bring me and them salvation leading to eternal life. Amen.

ex.w021: The phrase “Deo vivo et vero” also occurs in 1 Thessalonians 1:9.
